content.text: I have reproduced this, but only for in-domain resources. That is: the problem does not appear with URIs such as <
http://example.org/location#xywh=0,0,2034,2454
This points to the HttpResourceConverter class in fcrepo-http-commons as the culprit.
Thanks,
. Is it your belief that we should not be URL-encoding in-domain URLs?
https://www.ietf.org/rfc/rfc3986.txt
[2.4.  When to Encode or Decode]

I don't have a particular opinion related to RFC 3986, I was just noticing that we're being inconsistent. I would generally prefer that the URL representations are consistent. Does your reading of RFC 3986 suggest that our use of URL-encoded URIs is consistent with their guidelines?
Note also that URI.create(url) used in
FcrepoProducer
will throw a "java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: Illegal character in fragment".
EDIT:  This exception was rather caused by this URI:
http://localhost:8080/fcrepo/rest/collection/test/003/canvas/10#xywh&#61;1426,4053,279,47
which clearly has problems.  It seems that my code generated an HTML representation of an "=".   This has nothing to do with the ",".
I can work around the "," issue by just replacing the percent encoding in a SPARQL query, so having it encoded in the repository is OK for my use case.
It seems that this is
definitely
a problem that needs to be fixed in the Camel machinery. I would also like to see it fixed in Fedora core, so that, at the very least there is consistency in URI representations.
The percent encoding of reserved characters in a fragment problem I believe is a bug in
UriBuilder.fragment()

The docs say that it supports query parameters per RFC 3986, but apparently they have not considered the possibility of reserved characters in the value of a fragment.  Perhaps I raise the question to them directly?
This method is indeed used in
HttpResourceConverter

The variety of hash URI creation/manipulation in core is very confusing.  In the webapp, it seems that this is just using URI.create(uri) and not UriBuilder, which is why it works.  Also, the "internal" (/#/..) versus "external" (/#...) representation adds a lot of complexity.
Finally received response from java.com bug report filed here:
http://bugs.java.com/bugdatabase/view_bug.do?bug_id=JDK-8168268
Have resubmitted new issue here:
https://java.net/jira/browse/JAX_RS_SPEC-536
Testing this issue with Fedora 6.

curl -i -ufedoraAdmin:fedoraAdmin -XPUT -H"Content-type: text/turtle" -d " <_:e0c3ccbf985465c1f29a63ae9532ea3e> <http://www.w3.org/ns/oa#hasTarget> <http://localhost:8080/rest/collection/test/009/canvas/001#xywh=0,0,2137,3293> . <_:e0c3ccbf985465c1f29a63ae9532ea3e> <http://www.w3.org/ns/oa#hasTarget> <http://external.site/rest/collection/test/009/canvas/001#xywh=0,0,2137,3293> "
Results in an object that looks like
Not sure if that means we are good, but wanted to bring the findings back.
edit
*: Jira formatting is horrible.

In my humble opinion, this issue is resolved. It works in Fedora 6 (though we could add an integration test if desired) as expected by the original reporter. Also this issue is so old that no one is tracking it and the original Java issue link below points to a site which no longer exists.
We should confirm that this is no longer an issue with the latest Fedora java client.
Cannot replicate, may have been fixed by some other change.
If I have an RDF body triple that looks like this:
http://www.w3.org/ns/oa#hasTarget
http://localhost:8080/fcrepo/rest/collection/test/009/canvas/001#xywh=0,0,2137,3293
When the object value is created in Fedora, it looks like this:
http://localhost:8080/fcrepo/rest/collection/test/009/canvas/001#xywh=0%2C0%2C2137%2C3293
I should also point out that <
http://localhost:8080/fcrepo/rest/collection/test/009/canvas/001
> exists as an LDP Container prior to the update, and the hash is a schema specific identifier that is used by the client .
This happens both with FcrepoClient and directly with curl.  It does not occur if an update is made directly through the UI, however.
